claims.claim: Account management model for network APIs (Mastercom example): requesting access connects the customer to a regional Mastercard representative, and at implementation a named Mastercard Delivery Manager is assigned.
claims.quote: When you are ready for program implementation, you are assigned a Mastercard Delivery Manager who guides you through implementation.
claims.title: Support - Mastercom - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same page: access requests go to 'a regional Mastercard representative who provides further information about the Mastercom program'.

claims.claim: The public 'Get Help / Contact us for technical support' section on product Support pages is empty in the published markdown: the technical-support contact mechanism is rendered client-side and, per the portal's support page, requires sign-in.
claims.title: Support - Mastercom - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Identical empty heading on the Cross-Border Services Support page (same fetch). No hours, languages or response-time commitments appear on either page.

claims.claim: Mastercom publishes operational support parameters rather than SLAs: a throttling policy of 150 requests per second and a 120-second timeout.
claims.quote: The throttling policy is as follows: 150 requests per second.
claims.title: Support - Mastercom - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page also states 'Mastercom has a timeout set for 120 seconds.'

claims.claim: Credential hygiene is pushed onto the customer: Mastercom API keys expire every 13 months and customers are told they are responsible for tracking expiry and subscribing multiple users to lifecycle notifications.
claims.quote: Customers are responsible for tracking API key expiration.
claims.title: Support - Mastercom - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Recommends 'Subscribe multiple users to key lifecycle notifications (including expiration alerts) to avoid gaps in coverage.'

claims.claim: Deeper operational answers (dispute documentation windows, user guide) are deferred from the public Support page to the Chargeback Guide and Mastercom User Guide in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect, i.e. behind the customer login.
claims.quote: refer to the Chargeback Guide in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect.
claims.title: Support - Mastercom - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: BIN Lookup names a product-specific support mailbox and an 'assigned Account Manager' as the two support channels, including for pricing questions and for missed onboarding timelines.
claims.quote: For pricing details, contact your assigned Account Manager or send a query to DBN.BinTableResource.Support@mastercard.com.
claims.title: Support - BIN Lookup - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'For questions or if timelines are exceeded, contact the team at DBN.BinTableResource.Support@mastercard.com.'

claims.claim: Data-quality tickets for BIN Lookup have a defined intake format: account range, description of discrepancy, confirmation the issue reproduces on other cards with the same BIN, and reproduction steps.
claims.quote: Confirmation of checks on other cards with the same BIN
claims.title: Support - BIN Lookup - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Incident visibility for API products: Mastercard says BIN Lookup is synthetically monitored and that uptime and recent issues are publicly viewable on the developer.mastercard.com/api-status page.
claims.quote: The BIN Lookup API uses synthetic monitoring to continuously verify that the API is available and functioning as expected.
claims.title: Support - BIN Lookup - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page continues: 'This information is publicly available, allowing you to check uptime and review any recent issues.' The api-status URL itself returned only a JavaScript shell to curl (title 'Mastercard Developers').

claims.claim: Cross-Border Services support FAQ describes a three-tier environment path (Sandbox stubs, production-like MTF, Production) and states the sandbox cannot be used with OAuth 2.0 without registering as a Cross-Border customer, so pre-contract self-service is limited.
claims.quote: Currently, we don't support testing APIs in Sandbox using OAuth2.0 without registering for Mastercard Cross-Border Services.
claims.title: Support - Cross-Border Services - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same page: 'Sandbox has API stubs that return simulated, static responses. MTF is a production-like environment.'

claims.claim: Mastercard operates an Atlassian Statuspage (mastercard.statuspage.io, 'Mastercard Status') offering email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Atom and RSS incident subscriptions.
claims.quote: Get email notifications whenever Mastercard creates , updates or resolves an incident.
claims.title: Mastercard Status
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Email subscription is protected by OTP and reCAPTCHA; Slack and Teams webhook subscriptions offered.

claims.claim: The Statuspage appears to be an unpopulated template rather than a live incident channel: its only components are labelled '(example)' and every day in the past-incidents list reads 'No incidents reported'.
claims.title: Mastercard Status
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Past incidents section: 'Sep 25 , 2026 No incidents reported today. Sep 24 , 2026 No incidents reported.' Contrast with the api-status page promised on Mastercard Developers.

claims.claim: Mastercard's FY2025 10-K frames service-to-customers as an operational-resilience risk: disruptions that stop it processing transactions or servicing customers could materially affect the business.
claims.quote: Service disruptions that cause us to be unable to process transactions or service our customers could reduce our operational resilience
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: FY2025 10-K (period ending 2025-12-31). Post-dates Capital One's 2025-05-18 acquisition of Discover.

claims.claim: Incident response is described in the 10-K as an 'enterprise resiliency program' covering risk analysis, impact assessment and response strategies, with an explicit caveat that immunity cannot be ensured.
claims.quote: we maintain an enterprise resiliency program to analyze risk, assess potential impacts, and develop effective response strategies
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: The filing also notes 'We have experienced in limited instances, and may continue to experience, some types of these interruptions.'

claims.claim: A stated technology priority is to standardise how Mastercard connects with customers 'at the edge of the network' and give them self-service tools to manage and expand their Mastercard relationship.
claims.quote: to provide them with the tools to manage and expand their Mastercard relationship
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Full bullet: 'Standardizing and simplifying how we connect with customers, starting at the edge of our network, to provide them with the tools...'

claims.claim: Hands-on implementation support is sold as a paid services line (consulting and agentic solutions), not described as part of baseline network support.
claims.quote: strategic advisory, rapid prototyping, technical implementation and hands-on support across the payments ecosystem
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Listed under value-added services revenue categories.

claims.claim: Under the franchise model Mastercard sets performance standards and uses proactive monitoring of participant adherence to operating standards, the closest the 10-K comes to describing an SLA regime, and it runs one way (network monitoring customers).
claims.quote: use proactive monitoring designed to both ensure participant adherence to operating standards
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: No customer-facing service-level commitment, support hours or language coverage is stated anywhere in the 10-K.

claims.claim: BIN Lookup escalation for the daily SBART file and API keys points to the Mastercard Developers Dashboard and requires signing in and stating an intended use case on first access.
claims.quote: To access the SBART file, you must sign in to your Mastercard Developers account.
claims.title: Support - BIN Lookup - Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'When requesting access for the first time, you must provide a description of the intended use case.'
